newsitem.title: USA: Commerce's Daley hopeful on US, Japan trade picture.
newsitem.headline: Commerce's Daley hopeful on US, Japan trade picture.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said Thursday he is hopeful that the Japanese economy will start to grow and that there will be an improvement in the trade picture between the two countries.

"We feel pretty good that if the Japanese economy improves and there is continuing growth, I think if there is continuing reform in the economy, then we'll see an improvement -- as far as we are concerned -- in our exports," Daley told reporters before speaking to an Economic Strategy Institute conference.
When asked whether he thought trade friction would increase between the United States and Japan, Daley said "no."
Daley was also asked about a review of the U.S.-Japan automobile trade agreement. He said he would like to see that 1995 agreement "worked a little better."
But he declined to go into detail of what the U.S. review of the agreement will say. The Commerce Department and the U.S. Trade Representative's Office are scheduled to issue the report on Friday.
The Commerce Department reported Thursday that the February U.S. trade deficit with Japan declined by 0.9 percent to $4.26 billion.
